rawContent: @Boston_Married @wagatwe The focus on “power” also completely ignores the role of gender. So much of the #MeToo media coverage was about work hierarchies, but so much of this violence happens between people who would be “equal” if not for gender inequality.
These #MeToo apologies are everywhere--and most of them are actively harmful. Toobin's apology is no different. I shared some of my thoughts with USA Today. https://t.co/qui3YUyiFe
I really don't want to hear anyone say the #MeToo Movement has gone too far ever again.

One by one, we will spend the next ten years watching all of the men "canceled" by #MeToo come back. This time, with a broader base of supporters than they ever had before.

It's going to be excruciating.

I started to feel this shift toward the end of the #MeToo moment. In comparison to the horror stories of powerful serial perpetrators, survivors’ individual stories weren’t enough to capture anyone’s attention anymore. You needed more victims. More brutality.

For a couple of years there, almost everything I was asked to peer review was some academic trying to tie their work to #MeToo as a way to get more clicks.

Lately, everything I've been reading is good work by clear experts. THIS is the stuff that should be guiding policy.

Right around the time #MeToo went viral, theaters all over the country decided to run shows about sexual violence. It seems that very few of them considered there might already be very real histories of violence between cast members that might make this decision traumatic.
And to think--so many of the famous #MeToo stories were in the entertainment industry and it STILL didn't occur to any of these theaters that there might be perpetrators in their company.
